# System Data taxonomy

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:system-data` from src/systemData/catalog.ts and the en locale. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every location the System Data engine knows about, grouped as in the app. For what the safety levels mean, see the [expert guide](./README.md#the-safety-model).

- **Safe**: Regenerated automatically; removing it costs at most a rebuild or re-download and never loses user data.
- **Review**: Removal has a visible cost, or loses something that cannot be recreated (sign-outs, large re-downloads, device backups, emulator data). Offered, unselected by default, explained.
- **Advisory**: Reclaimable only through macOS or the owning tool. Shown with its size and the official command; never deleted by us.
- **Never**: Deleting it breaks macOS, an app or sync, or destroys user data. Always refused.

## User caches

| Target | Location | Safety | macOS | Needs FDA | Why | What regenerates it | Impact of removal | Handled by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| App caches | <code>Library/Caches/*</code> | Safe | any | no | Cache folders that third-party apps keep under Library/Caches to work faster. | Apps rebuild these automatically the next time they run. | Apps may start a little slower and re-download some data once. If the app is running, review it before removing. | System Data |
| Apple app and system caches | <code>Library/Caches/com.apple.*</code> | Review | any | no | Caches kept by Apple apps and background services. | macOS and the apps rebuild them as needed. | Some services download their data again, and apps like Safari lose their warm state until they rebuild it. | System Data |
| Sandboxed app caches | <code>Library/Containers/*/Data/Library/Caches</code> | Review | any | from macOS 14 | Caches inside the private container of an app from the App Store or another sandboxed app. | Each app recreates its cache when it needs it. | Apps may start slower and re-download data once. From macOS 14, reading other apps' containers needs Full Disk Access, so these are skipped without it. | System Data |
| Electron and Chromium app caches | <code>Library/Application Support/*/Cache</code><br><code>Library/Application Support/*/Code Cache</code><br><code>Library/Application Support/*/GPUCache</code><br><code>Library/Application Support/*/DawnCache</code><br><code>Library/Application Support/*/DawnGraphiteCache</code><br><code>Library/Application Support/*/DawnWebGPUCache</code><br><code>Library/Application Support/*/Service Worker/CacheStorage</code><br><code>Library/Application Support/*/CachedData</code><br><code>Library/Application Support/*/CachedExtensionVSIXs</code> | Safe | any | no | HTTP, shader and code caches of apps built on Chromium or Electron, such as Slack, VS Code or Discord. A Local State or Preferences file confirms the folder belongs to such an app. | The app rebuilds these caches on its next launch. | The app may open slower the first time. Quit the app first. | System Data |

## Never touched

Deleting it breaks macOS, an app or sync, or destroys user data. Always refused.

### Cloud storage files

iCloud Drive and file-provider data from services like Dropbox, OneDrive and Google Drive. Removing it can delete the only local copy of your files or cause sync conflicts.

- <code>Library/Mobile Documents/**</code>
- <code>Library/CloudStorage/**</code>

### Account and sync state

Folders under Caches that hold account, iCloud sync, Wallet and Home state, despite their location. Removing them can sign you out, force a full resync or break Wallet and Home.

- <code>Library/Caches/com.apple.bird/**</code>
- <code>Library/Caches/CloudKit/**</code>
- <code>Library/Caches/com.apple.akd/**</code>
- <code>Library/Caches/com.apple.amsaccountsd/**</code>
- <code>Library/Caches/com.apple.AuthenticationServices*/**</code>
- <code>Library/Caches/FamilyCircle/**</code>
- <code>Library/Caches/com.apple.HomeKit/**</code>
- <code>Library/Caches/PassKit/**</code>
- <code>Library/Caches/com.apple.passd/**</code>
- <code>Library/Caches/com.apple.iCloudHelper/**</code>

### Active downloads and open documents

Background downloads in progress and documents that are open or autosaved. Removing them can lose unsaved work or abort a download.

- <code>Library/Caches/com.apple.nsurlsessiond/**</code>
- <code>Library/Caches/TemporaryItems/**</code>

### Personal data and settings

Messages, Mail, Photos, Calendars, Contacts, Keychains, Cookies, Accounts and Preferences. This is your data and your settings, not a cache.

- <code>Library/Messages/**</code>
- <code>Library/Mail/**</code>
- <code>Library/Photos/**</code>
- <code>Library/Calendars/**</code>
- <code>Library/Application Support/AddressBook/**</code>
- <code>Library/Keychains/**</code>
- <code>Library/Cookies/**</code>
- <code>Library/Accounts/**</code>
- <code>Library/Preferences/**</code>

### App group containers

State shared between an app and its extensions, and protected by macOS from version 15. Removing it can break apps and their extensions.

- <code>Library/Group Containers/**</code>

### VM and model store internals

Docker's virtual disk, Colima VMs and Ollama's shared blobs and manifests. These are managed by their own tools, and deleting files by hand can destroy data or break other models.

- <code>Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data/vms/**</code>
- <code>.ollama/models/blobs/**</code>
- <code>.ollama/models/manifests/**</code>
- <code>.colima/**</code>

### Container folders

Parent folders such as Library, Caches and Application Support. Only their children can be offered, one at a time; a parent is never an item itself.

- <code>Library</code>
- <code>Library/Caches</code>
- <code>Library/Application Support</code>
- <code>Library/Containers</code>
- <code>Library/Application Support/MobileSync</code>
- <code>Library/Application Support/MobileSync/Backup</code>
- <code>Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Devices</code>

### macOS system files

System files, kernel extensions, system libraries, swap and sleep image, the Spotlight index, OS assets, updates and simulator runtime images. Removing them can make the Mac fail to start, break updates or corrupt Xcode.

- <code>/System/**</code>
- <code>/usr/lib/**</code>
- <code>/Library/Extensions/**</code>
- <code>/Library/Apple/**</code>
- <code>/private/var/vm/**</code>
- <code>/private/var/folders/**</code>
- <code>/.Spotlight-V100/**</code>
- <code>/private/var/MobileAsset/**</code>
- <code>/Library/Updates/**</code>
- <code>/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Volumes/**</code>
- <code>/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Images/**</code>
